entities.summary: Valery Alekseyevich Legasov was a Soviet inorganic chemist and a member of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union. He is primarily known for his efforts to contain the 1986 Chernobyl disaster. In August 1986, Legasov also presented the findings of an investigation to the International Atomic Energy Agency at the United Nations Office at Vienna, detailing the actions and circumstances that led to the explosion of Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant. Suffering from poor health because of radiation exposure, and frustrated that his attempts at reforming Soviet academic chemistry were rebuffed, he committed suicide in 1988.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Legasov's efforts to contain the Chernobyl disaster led to a significant shift in global nuclear safety regulations and practices, saving countless lives. His work also highlighted the need for greater transparency and accountability in scientific research.
